descriptor_candidates.name: log_length_mismatch_conf
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: For pure-silica zeolites at infinite dilution, the fraction of gas-phase entropy lost (1 - s_ads/s_gas) increases monotonically with the dimensionless ratio of the adsorbate's largest atomic span (GeDi, normalized by its training median) to the framework's largest free-sphere diameter (lsd_f, likewise normalized). The neural network, given this re-expression of the length mismatch, reduces MAE of entropy loss/R relative to raw-feature-only usage of the same information.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Confinement mechanism (known physical picture): when a molecule's geometric span approaches the free aperture of a channel or cage, cartwheel-type rotations and perpendicular translations are sterically hindered, so rotational/translational entropy loss grows (R1E08, R1E26, R1E29). Literature reports larger entropy loss in smaller-pore frameworks (FER vs FAU, MFI vs FAU); here the same mechanism is transferred to pure-silica rigid frameworks as a hypothesis, not an established law. The descriptor converts two independently median-normalized length ratios into a single dimensionless mismatch measure; its threshold of 1 has no physical equality meaning (q_GeDi and q_lsd_f use different references).
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: On training rows only: (a) within a declared native regime (e.g., lsd_f between its 10th and 90th training quantiles), the finite-difference derivative of the descriptor with respect to GeDi must be positive; (b) if the sign of the association between the descriptor and entropy loss/R is negative, or if feeding this single descriptor alongside the 14 native inputs does not reduce MAE versus the 14-input baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.

scientific_test.proxy_assumptions: GeDi proxies the adsorbate's maximum rotational/translational excursion; lsd_f proxies the limiting pore aperture. Both are static geometric proxies, not measures of lost freedom; lsd_f is a diameter, not an occupiable volume (unlike V_occ in R1E09/R1E10). Median-normalized ratios are dimensionless but do not preserve a physical threshold of 1.
scientific_test.physical_interpretation: Larger GeDi relative to the adsorbate population means a longer molecule; larger lsd_f means a more open framework. Their ratio is a pure geometric crowding index; equality of the two q-ratios does not imply GeDi equals lsd_f physically.

descriptor_candidates.name: geomean_q_inertia
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Because gas-phase rotational entropy scales as R*ln(sqrt(I_A I_B I_C)) plus a constant (R1E17), the geometric mean of the three median-normalized principal moments of inertia should correlate positively, and roughly logarithmically, with the entropy loss upon adsorption (entropy loss/R), with framework confinement modulating but not reversing the sign. Adding this descriptor to the 14 native inputs is hypothesized to reduce MAE of entropy loss/R on training data.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: This re-expresses the established statistical-mechanics rotational partition function (R1E17, R1E14) in dimensionless form; the relation itself is a known_relation, while its use as a single rankable descriptor for pure-silica systems is a new_combination. scientific_test.physical_interpretation: The geometric mean of q-PMIs is an effective dimensionless rotational size; a q-value of 1 means the molecule is at the training median, not that its inertia has a special physical value.

descriptor_candidates.name: planar_packing_ratio

Training MAE of entropy loss/R is hypothesized to decrease when this coupling descriptor is supplied in addition to the 14 native inputs.

descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: In pure-silica zeolites at infinite dilution, entropy loss/R depends on the composition of gas-phase entropy between rotational and translational modes, not only on its total: molecules whose rotational inertia is large relative to their mass (high log(q_PMI3/q_MW^1.5)) have a larger fraction of their gas entropy in rotational modes, and since framework-confinement preferentially removes rotational freedom while roughly one translational degree is lost regardless of framework (R2E03, R2E08, R2E11), such molecules should lose a larger fraction of gas entropy. The composition ratio is a new_combination as a descriptor; the underlying partition-function relations are established literature, not new discoveries. Inference: transfer from aluminosilicate frameworks and C3–C9 alkanes to pure-silica rigid frameworks at infinite dilution is explicitly hypothetical.

scientific_test.proxy_assumptions: PMI3 proxies the largest rigid-rotor inertia (ignoring symmetry number σ and flexibility); MW proxies translational entropy capacity as m^{3/2} per Sackur–Tetrode; framework rotational loss fraction F_rot is assumed transferable from aluminosilicate systems. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. Although these simulations are numerically cleaner compared to experiment because they involve analyzing efficiently a greater number of molecule–zeolite combinations, it remains overwhelming to apply them to the millions of hypothetical frameworks. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. Although these simulations are numerically cleaner compared to experiment because they involve analyzing efficiently a greater number of molecule–zeolite combinations, it remains overwhelming to apply them to the millions of hypothetical frameworks. Novel topology-based, data-driven approaches have been shown to be adequate in predicting specific features such as adsorption capacity $ ^{6} $ and selectivity. $ ^{26} $ However, there are currently no similar models for entropy.

retained.name: specific_wall_contact_ratio
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R increases with the specific surface-to-volume ratio LabuteASA/Vol of the adsorbate (units 1/angstrom): molecules with a larger exposed surface per unit volume make more wall-contact interactions per unit of retained bulk, and the accompanying vibrational/librational dampening of translations and rotations against pore walls removes a larger fraction of gas-phase entropy (R3E03, R3E10, R3E13). Because the fraction of gas-phase entropy lost is roughly fixed per framework while absolute loss grows with molecule size (R3E10), the SA/V shape factor re-expresses which part of the gas entropy is wall-coupled and should predict residual variation of entropy loss/R not captured by size alone. Adding this descriptor to the 14 native inputs reduces MAE of entropy loss/R versus the 14-input baseline.
